Before I jump into review, 339 GB with all DLCs? Damn, SSDs aren't exactly cheap these days and this game is asking from you space equal to 3-5 big games.

If I should start, why this review is negative and yet I am still playing it, well, it's fun with friends and some nice community. And to be honest, there simply isn't a competetion regarding this type of game. That doesn't mean I don't see everything what's wrong with this game each minute I am playing it and because of that new players simply should avoid buying this game, seriously. Studio Wildcard is one of the worst studios I've ever met and their monetization strategy is just horrible.

Also, let's check something, this is official info on Steam... "We're expecting to be in Early Access until the end of 2024." It's 2026 btw, just saying. Make picture which you want.

So, let's start with the positives. And those are definitely dinos. You have tons of them here and almost each one of them is helpful to you for different tasks. And it's fun. Many dinos have special taming strategy, some of them you won't be able to tame at low levels, some of them are here... just to be here I guess? But it's not wrong, not each dino has to have some purpose (even though, it's nice if they do). You have plenty of maps here, pretty big community around the game, official support of mods and Nekatus, which is author of the best maps in Ark.

And that's all for the positive side. So negatives? This is gonna be long one...

1) Official servers - straight from beginning, if you plan to play on official servers, simply don't. Players are crazy there but that's not the main issue. Those lags are actually even more insane. You are on server, where you should have 30 ms ping by their measures, yet that's not the part of the issue, because you are rubberbanding, traveling back in time and glitching yourself into textures every 5 seconds. Yea, it's not exaggerated, I mean it literally. For many players officials are simply not playable.

2) Mod "support" - ASA is officially supporting mods, mainly cosmetic ones, which server doesn't have to download, because games between players are sharing them with each other. Yet this is not something you could call "mod support". They have just special tab for mods (even paid ones, in EA, lol) in game with option to automatically download cosmetics from others, that's it. There ends the mod support (if I don't count that they regularly highlight some of them). 

Some mods are strictly required to play game at some comfy level, but the main issue are the cosmetic mods. They are nice but their stability, because of the game, is laughable. It happens to me every damn day that some mods, I previously downloaded, just won't load at all, even though they are blinking as "downloaded" and I have to re-download them. Some mods take 5 minutes to load. I mean, this is not a mod support, those are the same kind of issues you gonna experience in any game not officially supporting mods, which is sad.

3) PvP vs PvE - I am only PvE player, because PvP can be one of the most toxic encounters you gonna experience in games. Not even talking about the fact that the game simply isn't balanced around PvP at all. YouTube PvP videos are fun, but experiencing it on your own? If you don't have relatively big tribe, just give up, not worth of your time.

4) Optimization - I can't say a good thing about this one. You have to tweak your settings a lot until you gonna find something that suits you and your machine and that won't be enough either. I don't have issues on my PC on 1440p in any game, except for Ark. If you have already some decent base and few dinos out around your base, you are happy with 60-80 FPS in good times (with frame gen).

That said, a few weeks ago I bumped with my friend into cave where your FPS are getting eaten to 1 FPS, not joking, because of how many creatures spawn there. That's just insane and straight not playable. 

5) Graphics - so when it eats so many SSD space, it eats a lot CPU and GPU and RAM, it does have nice graphics, right? No, ASA is ported version of ASE on UE5 and there are definitely many and many models that've been here since ASE first release (or maybe even some testing versions). You can clearly see on some textures, either on maps or on dino models, that somebody was lazy and thought "nobody gonna notice that". Sadly, you gonna notice those things a lot. I mean, it doesn't have the worst graphics in the universe, most of it is fine but it simply isn't enough for how much resources the game is asking from you. It's a pure joke.

6) DLCs and P2W - ASA has jumped on a trend "let's make game P2W". Or at least for PvP players, in PvE you gonna notice it too, it just isn't a direct threat to you and your sessions. E.g. released DLC Dragontopia is just too OP. Dragons (mutated) are able to slay down even alpha king titan solo and laugh at it. Well, I guess it's a boosting mechanic, so the dragons at least fit into the game, right? No. They are straightly converted HTTYD models, which are a bit edited and that's it. I have that DLC and kinda enjoying the gameplay, but those models are just horrible and they don't fit into the game. Or, they are cute, they are nice but they are not "dinos into dino game" type of thing.

And don't let me start at Tides of Fortune DLC, which makes sure you have to buy it so you can properly enjoy Genesis map (which is just stupid).

-------------
Conclusion? Game is fun, mostly with friends, I wouldn't play this solo. But they ported ASE into new UE5 with ASE issues, fixed some of them and added a bunch of new ones, which they seem to not be bothered to fix. The right question is also "when this game gonna be released out of EA?", because as a player I am a bit worried. As soon as ASA started kicking, they completely dumped ASE even with their last DLC map, which is still broken to this day. So, the path for ASA gonna be the same? When Ark 2, maybe, gets released, we gonna stay in another game dead from devs' perspective?

If you want to play ASA, you have to count with issues from ASE and many more. You are simply buying game full of bugs, where most of them probably never gonna be fixed and with studio holding Wildcard very tightly, so they can milk the players. If you are fine with it, it can be fun. But if you can't stand to see bugs, glitches and issues with game every minute of your gaming sessions, simply avoid this game, because nobody from stable playerbase believes this gonna get better. And honestly? This is my last try with Ark. If Ark 2 gets released and this game won't be from at least 40% what it can be, I am simply not buying another Ark game. I have enough of promises and no results. Gonna enjoy ASA and do a big wave towards Ark 2, because I simply lost my faith in devs.

Another problem is the **huge file size**. The game takes up a massive amount of storage, and with additional content, maps, and updates, the required space can become ridiculous. The game needs better optimization not only for performance, but also for its overall storage requirements.

I really hope the developers focus on optimization, stability, bug fixing, and reducing unnecessary file size. ARK already has an incredible foundation, and it would be a shame to let technical problems hold it back.

To be clear, I don't think ARK: Survival Ascended is a bad game. **The game itself is excellent.** The problem is that its technical issues make it much harder to enjoy.

Please improve the optimization, fix the crashes and stuttering, and do something about the huge storage requirements.

I have recently completed an extensive scientific investigation into ARK: Survival Ascended, a game in which humanity has apparently survived extinction only to discover that civilization was a mistake and we should all go back to punching trees.

ARK is an astonishingly beautiful game. It has enormous landscapes, spectacular creatures, mysterious structures, different biomes, breeding, exploration, crafting, building, technology, and enough things to discover that for quite some time you fail to notice what you're actually doing.

You are gathering wood.

This is ARK's greatest achievement.

It disguises manual labor so magnificently that you can spend hours believing you're having an adventure when, in reality, you have accepted an unpaid position in the prehistoric lumber industry.

I discovered this when I acquired dinosaurs.

Naturally, I became attached to them. They had names. They had personalities. They had absolutely no understanding of personal safety. Consequently, I decided they needed a fence.

A fence.

Not a nuclear reactor. Not a space station. Not a scale replica of Versailles.

A fence.

ARK examined this modest request and apparently concluded that every tree visible from orbit should die in order to build it.

So I started chopping.

Eventually, I learned that there is a beaver.

Wonderful!

The beaver gathers wood.

This seemed like precisely the technological breakthrough my emerging civilization required, except there was a small problem: obtaining the beaver required progressing far enough to acquire the appropriate equipment and resources to tame the beaver efficiently.To reach the beaver, you must brave crocodiles, Rexes, and several deeply upsetting creatures you didn't even know existed until they emerged from the vegetation with strong opinions about your continued existence. You are, of course, spectacularly unequipped to defend yourself against any of them because you haven't progressed far enough to make the equipment you need.

And why haven't you progressed far enough?

Because you need wood.

And what did I have to do while progressing toward the magnificent wood-gathering beaver?

Gather wood.

At some point I realized that by the time I acquired an animal capable of helping me build the fence, I could simply have deforested half the map by myself and eventually finished building the fence.

This is when I began to understand ARK.

ARK has progression, but much of that progression allows you to become progressively better at doing the things you have already been doing because you need to do even more of them.

You gather resources so you can make equipment.

The equipment helps you gather resources.

Those resources allow you to tame creatures.

Some creatures help you gather resources.

Those resources allow you to build better equipment and structures.

Which require more resources.

Eventually, you stand on a hill surrounded by dinosaurs, industrial machinery and enough technological advancement to frighten NASA, and somehow you're still worried about whether you have enough fiber.

There are specialized dinosaurs that can help.

One gathers berries magnificently.

This would have been tremendously exciting had I ever experienced a berry emergency.

The resources I desperately wanted assistance with, naturally, were generally the ones requiring an expedition involving specialized equipment, dangerous terrain, several predators and the distinct possibility that I would return home without whatever I went looking for but with fourteen unrelated objects and a new dinosaur.

And this is the genius of ARK: **it is repetitive, but it is extraordinarily good at hiding it.**

There is always something in the distance.

A mountain.

An obelisk.

A strange animal.

A coastline.

A swamp.

A snow-covered region.

Something enormous flying overhead that makes you reconsider leaving the house.

You go investigate, something ridiculous happens, and suddenly three hours have passed and you've forgotten that the reason you left home was because you needed metal.

Then you return home.

You need wood.

ARK is not a bad game. Quite the opposite. A bad game could never have persuaded me to participate willingly in this much manual labor.

ARK is a brilliant game constructed around a fundamental economic principle:

**Whatever you want, you don't have enough of it.**

Want a bigger house?

Wood.

Want a fence?

Wood.

Want equipment?

Resources.

Want better equipment?

More resources.

Want a creature that gathers resources?

Excellent. Please gather some resources so you can obtain it.

There are bosses, caves and enormous amounts of content for players interested in those things. There are multiple maps that could theoretically keep someone occupied until retirement.

But eventually I looked at those other maps and had a terrifying realization.

I could start again.

I could wake up on another magnificent beach.

I could explore another spectacular world.

I could discover entirely different creatures.

And then...

I could gather wood.

That was the moment my pioneering spirit died.

ARK: Survival Ascended gave me beautiful scenery, beloved animals, genuine adventures, moments of absolute panic, several inexplicable disasters and more entertainment than I expected.

It also taught me something important about myself.

If civilization ever collapses and humanity genuinely has to start over from sticks and stones, I have made my decision.

I am not rebuilding it.

Someone else can get the wood.

I genuinely wanted to like ARK: Survival Ascended, but the performance alone makes it incredibly difficult to recommend.

Despite having a fairly powerful PC, this game ran like utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The performance is all over the place, and the fact that a game can look this rough while running this poorly is honestly impressive in the worst possible way. I shouldn't have to fight the game itself just to maintain a playable framerate.

And then there's the fact that ASA just feels completely different from the original ARK. Obviously, some changes are expected with a remake/remaster, but a lot of the things that made the original feel intuitive now feel awkward or unnecessarily complicated.

The keybinds are an absolute mess. Yes, you can change them, but the fact that you basically have to spend time fixing the controls before the game feels remotely comfortable is ridiculous. Some controls just don't feel like they were designed with the same thought as the original.

Overall, ARK: Survival Ascended feels like a game that should have been a massive improvement over its predecessor, but instead feels like I'm constantly compromising between performance, controls, and actually enjoying the game.

If you already own the original ARK, I'm not convinced ASA is worth the upgrade unless you specifically want the visual overhaul and are willing to put up with the performance issues.

If you are someone that worries about storage as well I believe this game takes roughly 200+ GB for just the base game. I would imagine if you got every DLC on top of that it is easily going to reach a minimum of 300GB

What's unfortunate is the mechanic itself with taming dinos, base building etc. in the world they made sounds exciting especially when you see these amazing looking images and trailers on the store page and I genuinely wanted to dive into this title. However, that falls short once you actually dive in. Who knows maybe one day this game will get to a state of optimization and performance while achieving in my opinion, high fidelity comparable to that of a modern day current Gen game title and not need me to research performance mods etc... to achieve that. 

Mods should be for fun and optional not feel like a necessity.

Then the game crashes.

You load back in.

Your dinosaur is dead.
Your base is gone.
Your will to live is questionable.

Then Steam says:

"ARK has an update."

Of course it does.

At this point, I'm not surviving on the ARK.

Still playing though.
